scope.focus: Server-Side Request Forgery (CWE-918 primary, per user instruction)

project_purpose: Label Studio is an open-source multi-type data-labeling/annotation tool. It runs a Django web server (entry points: `label-studio` CLI -> label_studio/server.py:main, and manage.py) exposing a Django REST Framework API under /api/ (projects, tasks, import, export, storage backends, ML backends, webhooks). Annotators/project collaborators import tasks (files or URLs), connect external cloud storage (S3/GCS/Azure/Redis/local files), attach machine-learning backends (HTTP services) for predictions/training, and register webhooks that the server POSTs to on annotation events. These import-by-URL, ML-backend, webhook, and storage-endpoint features are exactly the surfaces where the server issues outbound network requests driven by API-supplied values.

framework_notes: Django + Django REST Framework is the primary stack (score 1.00 / 0.90). references/django.md was loaded in addition to references/python.md and references/patterns.md.

IMPORTANT scope fact: this CodeQL database contains ONLY the label_studio application package (~33k LOC). Django itself, DRF, requests, boto3, redis-py, google-cloud-storage are external pip dependencies whose sources are NOT in the database. Extraction therefore anchors on application-level call sites (urlopen call in data_import, requests.* calls in webhooks/ml/core utils, boto3/redis client construction in io_storages) and on DRF request-object attribute reads, not on framework internals.

All API endpoints require authentication (DRF Token/session; core/settings). Endpoint-level permissions observed: ImportAPI = projects_change (data_import/api.py:172), MLBackendListAPI = projects_change (ml/api.py:78), WebhookListAPI = IsAuthenticated + organization membership (webhooks/api.py:58-60), ImportStorageListAPI = projects_change (io_storages/api.py:26). These are project-collaborator level, NOT admin-only: any authenticated user with project-change rights (or, for webhooks, any organization member) can supply the URLs that reach the network sinks. Permission checks limit attacker identity but not the trust level of the URL values themselves (per references/django.md middleware/auth note).

Three genuine user-driven outbound-HTTP flows exist: (1) task import by URL: POST /api/projects/{pk}/import with form body url= -> load_tasks (uploader.py:143) -> tasks_from_url (uploader.py:114) -> urlopen(url) (uploader.py:123) with SSL certificate verification disabled (ctx.check_hostname=False, ctx.verify_mode=ssl.CERT_NONE, lines 118-120) and an optional url_is_local guard gated by settings.SSRF_PROTECTION_ENABLED (line 175); (2) webhook delivery: Webhook.url/headers written by any organization member via /api/webhooks (no local-IP check) -> requests.post(webhook.url, headers=webhook.headers, ...) (webhooks/utils.py:24); (3) ML backend calls: MLBackend.url written via /api/ml (validate_url applies url_is_local only when settings.ML_BLOCK_LOCAL_IP is true, ml/serializers.py:10-13) -> MLApi(BaseHTTPAPI) -> requests.Session.request (ml/api_connector.py:81-83), with URL suffixes joined via urllib.parse.urljoin (api_connector.py:132).

Fixed-destination outbound HTTP (FP material for CWE-918 but recorded for completeness): pypi.org version check (core/utils/common.py:362), tele.labelstud.io telemetry (core/utils/contextlog.py:177, URL is a literal), sqlite.org dll download at startup with verify=False (core/utils/windows_sqlite_fix/__init__.py:26, Windows-only, URL built from a constant filename).

Non-HTTP network connections recorded separately: boto3 S3 client/resource with API-suppliable endpoint_url (io_storages/s3/utils.py:40-41), redis.StrictRedis with API-suppliable host/port (io_storages/redis/models.py:57), socket.gethostbyname inside the url_is_local guard (core/utils/io.py:177, DNS resolution performed by the sanitizer check itself).
Redirect-producing Django responses are client-side navigation (Pass 9 / CWE-601 material) and are NOT extracted as CWE-918 sinks; the RedirectView at core/urls.py:49 targets a fixed path.

url_is_local (core/utils/io.py:171-192) is a sanitizer candidate: resolves the hostname via socket.gethostbyname then rejects 0.0.0.0 and the four RFC1918-style private subnets. It is applied to the import URL (uploader.py:175, gated by settings.SSRF_PROTECTION_ENABLED) and to ML backend URLs (ml/serializers.py:10-13, gated by settings.ML_BLOCK_LOCAL_IP). Webhook URLs have no such check. Its check-then-fetch structure (separate DNS resolution in url_is_local vs. the later fetch in urlopen) is a TOCTOU shape that the labeling/analysis stages should keep in mind, but that does not affect candidate extraction.

coverage_gaps: Django / DRF / requests / boto3 / redis-py / google-cloud-storage / azure-storage-blob library internals are NOT in this database (only label_studio application code, ~33k LOC). The final network I/O of requests.Session.request, boto3's HTTP stack, and redis-py lives in external libraries; sinks are therefore anchored at the application call sites (self.http.request(...), session.client('s3', ...), redis.StrictRedis(...)), and taint must reach those call sites' arguments to be reported.

requests keyword-form URL arguments: contextlog.py:177 passes the URL as keyword url= to requests.post (a hardcoded literal, no taint value); the extraction records keyword-form requests.get/post calls with argIndex -1. For webhooks/utils.py:24 and common.py:362 / windows_sqlite_fix:26 the URL is positional argument 0 and argIndex is 0. Call.getArg(int) cannot read keyword arguments; flows that reach requests.* calls via keyword `url=` other than the literal at contextlog.py:177 would need keyword-argument modeling in later stages.

DB-mediated flows (webhook.url, MLBackend.url, S3ImportStorage.s3_endpoint, Redis host/port) cross HTTP requests (written via one API request, used in a later request or background signal). Intra-procedure/inter-procedure taint analysis cannot bridge the database; these are extracted as field-read sources (webhook.url, self.url, self.s3_endpoint, self.host/port) so the pass-3 taint query can still link them to the sinks, mirroring the 'DB content reused into sinks' source family from references/patterns.md.

DRF serializer internals (validated_data materialization) are framework code outside this database; serializer field entry points are approximated by extracting the validated field handlers that exist in application code (MLBackendSerializer.validate_url parameter, attrs['url'] subscript in ml/serializers.py) and by the request.data attribute-read source family.
webhooks/models.py imports requests but never calls it (unused import); no sink is emitted for it.

gcs/models.py:176 requests.Request() is object construction for google-auth credential signing, not network I/O; not extracted as a sink. GCS/Azure presigned-URL generation returns URLs to the browser without a server-side fetch - not CWE-918 sinks.

socket.gethostbyname in core/utils/io.py:177 is the DNS lookup inside the url_is_local sanitizer guard (its domain argument is user-controlled, but its purpose is validation); recorded as a sanitizer candidate in framework_notes, not as a sink.
